name: MonarchBanner
title: Alert
summary: An inline status message with a tone, an optional title, a message and one optional action.
whenToUse: For a status that belongs to the content on screen and should stay visible.
whenNotToUse: For a message that must interrupt, use the system alert modifier. For a transient confirmation, do not use a banner.
api: init(_ title: String? = nil, message: String? = nil, tone: MonarchTone = .info, toneLabel: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, actionTitle: String? = nil, action: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
init<Actions: View>(_ title: String? = nil, message: String? = nil, tone: MonarchTone = .info, toneLabel: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

options.name: message
options.description: The message; nil for a banner that is only a title.

options.name: tone
options.description: Selects the colours and the icon.

options.name: toneLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name of the tone.

options.name: systemImage
options.description: Replaces the tone's SF Symbol; the tone still sets the colours and the spoken name.

options.name: actions
options.description: Several actions, in a row that stacks when it does not fit.

options.name: actionTitle
options.description: Title of the action button. No button without it.

options.name: action
options.description: Runs when the action button is activated.

appearance: A tinted container with a border and 12-point corners; the icon is in the strong colour of the tone and the text in the default text colour.
platformNotes: Named MonarchBanner on both native platforms because alert means a modal dialog on iOS and Android; the web component is Alert. The web's live-region option has no direct equivalent, so the app posts an announcement when it inserts a banner. The actions sit on the trailing edge, as on the web. The tone symbols follow the web alert: the warning triangle for danger too.
accessibility: The icon, title and message are one element, read as the tone name, the title, then the message.
The tone name is spoken, so the tone does not depend on colour or the icon; it can be replaced with toneLabel.
The action is a separate button with a touch target of at least 44 points.
The banner does not announce itself when it appears.
edgeCases: The neutral tone has no spoken tone name.
actionTitle without action, or action without actionTitle, shows no button.

examples.title: Tones

parityExceptions.reason: MonarchBanner on iOS has no live-region option: a banner does not announce itself.
parityExceptions.convention: SwiftUI announces with AccessibilityNotification.Announcement, which the app posts when it inserts the banner.
